Decision: Kyoto skeletal widths in millimetres at CRL: shoulder 16.6 mm, hips 6.7 mm, with 22.5 and 9.2 mm as upper bounds. Applied at the growth chart rewrite. See LIKELY_SOURCEABLE.md.

item: The fetus is pinned in the womb and the fluid is nearly absent: the 23 joints are neck, spine and limbs only, so the trunk cannot translate or turn; only limb spheres are tested against the uterine wall (head and trunk never touch it); fluid drag is a slow-flow term with a hard-coded viscosity 1e-3 that adds nothing visible to joint damping; net weight is built and sourced but no recording passes a gravity direction; no added mass; the cord does not tether; the wall keeps its shape
why: Read on the built 12.5 week body (scratch float_check.py, 2026-11-13): volume 11.15 mL, mass 11.71 g, net weight 2.6e-3 N. On the pinned trunk, net weight shifts a joint by 1.8 deg at most (neck) and drag is negligible, so switching them on changes little. Free, the body would sink at about 130 mm/s (net weight against speed-squared drag, coefficient 0.5 assumed) and rest on the lowest wall; a limb push of 0.02-0.1 N for 0.1 s would move it 6-28 mm in a cavity of 27.7 mm half-width, where slow-flow drag is 70-330 times smaller than speed-squared drag. So wall touch, hand-face contact counts and the afferent reading all depend on a free body. Estimates, not sourced values
resolve: One build, in order: (1) source first: a drag law for a bluff body at Reynolds 100-20,000 (lead: Morrison 2013 sphere correlation; Schiller-Naumann 1933), added mass of a body in fluid, amniotic fluid viscosity (one search: only microviscosity found), cord length and stiffness at 12.5 weeks, wall force law (M-096); (2) six root freedoms, appended after the jaw joints so existing joint indices keep their place, implemented as the wall moving in the trunk frame; (3) head and trunk primitives against the wall; (4) net weight on in every recording, direction drawn per run; (5) speed-squared drag and added mass on the whole body; (6) numba mirror and the body tests; (7) re-record. No code before step 1 is read and bound
evidence: Equal-length result 2026-11-14 (section 19): free body with coupled wall contact, 240 s, seeds 7-9: touch reading 0.119-0.179 (pinned 0.108-0.160), general movements 4.8-16.4% (pinned 4.6-11.2%, source 6-18), movement time toward the face 0.50 s unchanged; earlier 180 s comparisons (sections 17-18) were unequal and are corrected. Method: a body-part map recovered from resting-state correlation seeded in each sensory body-part region; fluctuations strongest at rest, quenched during movement, absent in corticospinal output. Data CC-BY at doi:10.25452/figshare.plus.28633379; code github.com/hillmanlab/M2-topography (Zenodo doi:10.5281/zenodo.23605411).
why: gives a brain-lane analysis for the touch reading: seed correlations computed in rest periods only, and sensory-to-motor homology as a map test
resolve: add a rest-only variant to b2_raw (movement periods from gm_score masked) and a seed map from skin afferent units to motor pools; hypothesis only, no constant changes
evidence: Finding stated (2026-11-14): in adult mice the paper finds a body-part map in M2 with the touch map's layout, read from resting correlations seeded in each S1 body-part region, confirmed by Allen atlas axonal tracing and by body-part-specific M2 activity in spontaneous movement. The model has no M2 counterpart (one touch map at the trigeminal level; join J10 rejects a movement copy for Phase 1). USER asked to test as a priority whether touch and motor pools already line up per body part at rest: pre-registered in companion/audit_log/verification/research_grade_2026-11-09/HOMOLOGY_PREREG_2026-11-14.md, scorer homology_score.py; recording with muscle activation queued after the M-104 recording.

item: Hypothesis lead (USER question 2026-11-14, resonance and harmonics for the learner): precedent checked via Europe PMC/Crossref. Movement-driven oscillations organise early body maps: 'Early motor activity drives spindle bursts in the developing somatosensory cortex', R. Khazipov, 2004, Nature, doi:10.1038/nature03132 (newborn rats); 'Rapid cortical oscillations and early motor activity in premature human neonate', M. Milh, 2007, Cerebral Cortex, doi:10.1093/cercor/bhl069 (preterm humans). Cell level: 'Resonate-and-fire neurons', E. M. Izhikevich, 2001, Neural Networks, doi:10.1016/s0893-6080(01)00078-8. Analysis: 'Human brain networks function in connectome-specific harmonic waves', S. Atasoy, 2016, Nat Commun, doi:10.1038/ncomms10340 (adult). Learning theory: 'Adaptive Resonance Theory...', S. Grossberg, 2013, Neural Netw, doi:10.1016/j.neunet.2012.09.017 (cognitive model, not a fetal mechanism). Stochastic resonance at the afferent already in CF2_CELL_SPEC (Collins 1996, [M, verify]).
why: all precedent is cortical, postnatal or adult; none places resonance in the 12.5 week brainstem learner
resolve: search fetal or neonatal brainstem (trigeminal, cuneate) oscillations tied to movement; read Khazipov 2004 and Milh 2007 in full; hypothesis only until a fetal-brainstem source
evidence: 2026-11-14: rhythmic structure in the body's own input is sourced in the human fetus at the stage: de Vries 1985 (Early Hum Dev, doi:10.1016/0378-3782(85)90174-4, abstract): breathing movements with a preferred interval of 2-3 s at 10 weeks, under 1 s by 19 weeks; hiccups every 1-3 s; isolated arm movements about every 1 s.

item: Design direction (USER 2026-11-14): replace the learner's prediction structure (Asabuki and Clopath 2024 predictive E-I network) with a model built only from neural and synaptic correlates of resonance: neurons with intrinsic frequency preference, synapses that strengthen when activity locks in phase, a body map formed from self-generated correlated activity. Precedent checked via Europe PMC/Crossref: 'Resonance, oscillation and the intrinsic frequency preferences of neurons', B. Hutcheon, 2000, Trends Neurosci, doi:10.1016/s0166-2236(00)01547-2; 'Oscillatory Neurocomputers with Dynamic Connectivity', F. C. Hoppensteadt, 1999, Phys Rev Lett, doi:10.1103/physrevlett.82.2983 (oscillators interact and learn only when their frequencies match); 'Spontaneous muscle twitches during sleep guide spinal self-organization', P. Petersson, 2003, Nature, doi:10.1038/nature01719 (neonatal rat body-map reflex modules self-organise from twitches, no learning objective); 'Synaptic activity and the construction of cortical circuits', L. C. Katz, 1996, Science, doi:10.1126/science.274.5290.1133; 'Visual feature integration and the temporal correlation hypothesis', W. Singer, 1995, Annu Rev Neurosci, doi:10.1146/annurev.ne.18.030195.003011; 'Geometric constraints on human brain function', J. C. Pang, 2023, Nature, doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06098-1 (adult, descriptive).
why: no published learner maps a body by resonance alone; parts exist (cell resonance, phase-locked plasticity, twitch-driven self-organisation); fetal-stage evidence for the parts is missing
resolve: source methods before any code: (1) intrinsic resonance currents (HCN / Ih, M-current) in fetal or neonatal brainstem touch relays at 12.5 weeks or nearest; (2) a phase- or timing-dependent plasticity rule from developing sensory synapses; (3) read Petersson 2003 and Hoppensteadt 1999 in full and list each method; then a pre-registered probe against the current learner on the same recordings
evidence: 2026-11-14: relay_map.py (PA2 van Ooyen 1999 read from the PDF and bound K18; PA4; PA5) and reflex_learner.py (PB2) built; test_phase1_learner.py passes: TR1, TR2 (mismatch recorded), van Ooyen Fig 5a/5b reproduced, PA4, Petersson simulation reproduced (r 0.955-0.973 against 0.85-0.94); provenance unchanged, isolation and master pass. Not yet built: substrate neuron (RS1 equations to read), STP, multi-target relay, closed-loop reflex wiring.

item: Vestibular input misses whole-body rotation in the free body (found 2026-11-14): transduction7 takes the head's angular velocity as the two neck joint rates because the thorax was body7's fixed frame; with Body7(free=True) the trunk rotates (root angular velocity rw, tens of degrees per second while settling), and the canals should sense head rotation = root rotation plus neck rotation. No otolith (linear acceleration or gravity) input either, as in v6.

resolve: in free mode, hand over the head's angular velocity as rw (womb frame, rotated into the head frame) plus the neck rates; check the transducer law's source covers whole-head rotation; re-record
evidence: Code fix in place (transduction7.head_state adds root rotation along the neck axes in free mode; cost 0.01 ms per call). The 240 s recording m104_vest_240s is identical in events and scores to m104_coupled_240s because the vestibular pathway is disconnected (K_VEST 0, VEST_nuc has no outputs; see M-110).

resolve: source the fetal vestibular afferent gain and the vestibular nucleus projections at 12.5 weeks before setting K_VEST or wiring VEST_nuc; then re-record

item: No fetal breathing or hiccup movements in the model (found 2026-11-14): no breathing or hiccup generator in the brainstem and no chest or diaphragm DOF in Body7. Human fetal breathing movements run from about 10 weeks with a preferred interval of 2-3 s, hiccups every 1-3 s (de Vries 1985, doi:10.1016/0378-3782(85)90174-4); a brainstem breathing rhythm generator starts at mouse E15 = 12.5 weeks (Thoby-Brisson 2005, doi:10.1523/jneurosci.0551-05.2005; embryonic pacemaker currents: Chevalier 2016, doi:10.7554/elife.16125).
why: the learner design (RESONANT_LEARNER_DESIGN_V3.md section 3) takes the body's rhythms as the harmonic drive; the best-sourced rhythm at the stage is absent
resolve: source fetal breathing movement kinematics (chest and abdominal wall excursion, diaphragm) and rate at 10-13 weeks, add a breathing DOF to the body and a sourced embryonic rhythm generator to the brainstem; check the rate against de Vries 1985
evidence: Proposal written 2026-11-14 (design v3 section 3c): breathing DOF (chest and abdominal wall excursion) plus a brainstem rhythm generator outside the learner (form from Thoby-Brisson 2005, Chevalier 2016), hiccups as recurring events; tests against de Vries 1985 intervals; values pending the gap-solutions research.

item: Slowly adapting (SA-I) afferents at 12.5 weeks are not supported by stage data (found 2026-11-14): at rat E15-E20, 97.5% of trigeminal ganglion cells give rapidly adapting responses to innocuous touch and 94.3% are silent without stimulation; 89% of vibrissa-related cells respond to one follicle only; 64% show rapid response decrement ('Prenatal development of the receptive fields of individual trigeminal ganglion cells in the rat', N.
